meaning: The number 144,000 symbolizes the chosen and sealed servants of God, representing completeness and wholeness in God's plan of salvation.
description: In Revelation 7:4 the 144000 are described as the sealed ones from all twelve tribes of Israel – 12000 from each tribe. The number is the product of 12 × 12 × 1000, where 12 symbolizes God’s people and 1000 represents a large complete multitude. In Revelation 14:1 the 144000 appear again, now standing together with the Lamb on Mount Zion, with his name and his Father’s name written on their foreheads. They sing a new song that no one else can learn – only those who have been bought from the earth (Rev 14:3). Many theologians interpret the number symbolically rather than literally, as an expression of the complete multitude of all God’s chosen people throughout history, where the sealing and the new song emphasize their special belonging to God and the Lamb.

versions.description: In Revelation 7:4, the 144,000 are described as those sealed from all twelve tribes of Israel—12,000 from each tribe. The number is the product of 12 × 12 × 1,000, where 12 symbolizes God's people (twelve tribes and twelve apostles) and 1,000 represents a vast, complete multitude. In Jewish tradition, the number twelve is linked to the tribes of Israel and God's covenant relationship with His people. Many theologians interpret the number symbolically rather than literally, as an expression of the complete assembly of all of God's chosen throughout history.

footnotes.text: The mathematical structure 12 × 12 × 1,000 unites the symbolism of both covenants: twelve tribes (the old covenant) and twelve apostles (the new covenant), multiplied by 1,000, which in biblical context denotes an immeasurable yet complete multitude (cf. Ps 50:10; Deut 7:9).

In Jewish tradition, the number twelve is deeply connected to the tribes of Israel and God's covenant relationship with His people. The twelve tribes represent the entirety of God's chosen people, and thus the number 144,000 can be understood as a perfection of this wholeness.

There is significant theological debate regarding the relationship between the 144,000 in Revelation 7 and 14. Some view them as identical groups described from different perspectives—first sealed on earth (chapter 7), then victorious in heaven (chapter 14). Others see them as two distinct groups. Additionally, there is discussion about whether the number is literal (only Jewish believers) or symbolic (all of God's people from every nation).
